articles.title: 'Nayyi Navelli' OTT release: Here's where to watch Yami Gautam Dhar's horror comedy after the theatrical run
articles.summary: Spoiler Alert: This article contains main plot details and spoilers for 'Drishyam 3'.
articles.body: Spoiler Alert: This article contains main plot details and spoilers for 'Drishyam 3'. If you haven't seen the film yet and wish to avoid spoilers, please stop reading now.Yami Gautam Dhar's horror comedy 'Nayyi Navelli' is set to reach audiences on OTT after its theatrical run. The movie arrived in theaters on October 16, 2026, giving audiences their first opportunity to watch its mix of supernatural incidents, family drama and humor on the big screen.'Nayyi Navelli' OTT release date and platformThe film's official posters identify Amazon Prime Video as its OTT partner, although the exact release date remains unknown. Set in Meerut, 'Nayyi Navelli' follows a woman whose arrival in her marital home takes an unexpected turn. Yami Gautam Dhar plays a bride who initially appears to be a welcome addition to the family. However, her brother-in-law begins to suspect that she may be a witch, creating tension despite her husband's and in-laws' affection for her. The story takes a stranger turn when her husband transforms into a monster. This supernatural development is connected to Kaal Sheel which is a mysterious stone believed to date back to the Treta Yuga. The movie has a 'Stree'- touch in it's story narrative as it combines humor and horror elements.'Nayyi Navelli' box office collectionThe film began its theatrical run on October 16, 2026. According to Sacnilk, it collected Rs 3.25 cr in India net earnings on its opening day. Its domestic gross stood at Rs 3.83 cr, while overseas markets contributed Rs 75 lakh. These figures took the film's worldwide gross collection to Rs 4.58 cr on Day 1.Cast and crew of 'Nayyi Navelli'Directed by Balaji Mohan and written by Himanshu Sharma, the film features Yami Gautam Dhar in the lead role. The supporting cast includes Addinath Kothare, Anurag Thakur, Mita Vashishth, Sonal Jha, Sunita Rajwar, Sushmita Mukherjee, Aaditya Kulshresth and Suneel Sinha.

articles.title: Iran helping Houthis: How Tehran is hitting Saudi Arabia without fighting directly
articles.summary: Iran has provided Yemen’s Houthi rebels with intelligence and tactical guidance to help them target Saudi Arabia and forces allied with Riyadh, according
articles.body: Iran has provided Yemen’s Houthi rebels with intelligence and tactical guidance to help them target Saudi Arabia and forces allied with Riyadh, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal, raising concerns about Tehran’s growing role in the conflict and the threat to regional security.According to WSJ report, Iranian assistance has extended beyond weapons supplies to intelligence-sharing and operational support. The allegations point to closer coordination between Tehran and the Houthis as the group intensifies its military campaign against Saudi Arabia.The support the Houthis received from Iran and other Axis actors “undeniably paved the way for the rapid-fire gains they’ve made over the past few months,” Adam Baron, a Yemen expert and fellow at the Washington-based policy institute New America, told the WSJ.Iran’s assistance reportedly includes intelligence to identify targets, training in operating advanced weapons, tactical guidance and help developing locally manufactured drones and missiles.The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and Lebanon’s Hezbollah have helped the Houthis acquire technical expertise in missile systems and weapons production, according to experts cited by Reuters.The assistance is also intended to reduce the Houthis’ dependence on direct weapons shipments from Iran.Andreas Krieg, a senior security studies lecturer at King’s College London, said, “Tehran has not simply supplied the Houthis with weapons. It has helped create an indigenous military-industrial learning process that becomes progressively harder to dismantle, even if direct Iranian supply routes are disrupted.”Danny Citrinowicz, a former head of the Iran branch of Israeli defence intelligence, told the WSJ that the operational relationship between Tehran and the Houthis was “very, very strong”.“Iran has a major interest in the Houthis’ success,” Citrinowicz said, adding that the attacks harm Saudi Arabia and push up oil prices. He described the relationship as one based on “strategic cooperation” rather than a conventional client-patron arrangement.Iran and the Houthis’ relationshipThe relationship between Iran and Yemen’s Houthis developed from shared political interests into a closer military partnership over the past two decades.The Houthis emerged in northern Yemen during the 1990s as a movement rooted in the Zaydi branch of Shia Islam and began fighting the Yemeni government in 2004.Iran’s support expanded as Yemen’s political crisis deepened following the 2011 Arab Spring and the Houthis strengthened their position against the government.In March 2015, Saudi Arabia led a military coalition to support Yemen’s internationally recognised government and push back against the rebels, turning the conflict into a major regional confrontation involving Riyadh and Tehran.Iran’s military assistance to the Houthis grew during the war, including reported supplies of missiles, drones, training and technical expertise.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Truly historic moment’: Putin’s envoy hails Trump’s move to suspend Russia sanctions
articles.summary: Russian president’s Vladimir Putin investment envoy Kirill Dmitriev has described US president Donald Trump’s decision to waive a fresh package of
articles.body: Russian president’s Vladimir Putin investment envoy Kirill Dmitriev has described US president Donald Trump’s decision to waive a fresh package of sanctions and tariffs against Russia as a “truly historic moment”. The remarks came after Washington suspended key provisions of legislation aimed at tightening economic pressure on Moscow over its war in Ukraine."The suspension of some of the provisions of the Graham Act marks an important and truly historic moment," Dmitriev said in a post on X on Saturday.The remarks came a day after the White House released an executive order in which Trump said the waiver was in the national interest of the United States. The measures had been due to take effect under the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which Trump signed in mid-September.In his post, Dmitriev argued that the legislation could have severely disrupted economic ties between the two countries."The legislation, which underwent fundamental and deeply negative changes following Senator Graham's death, could have effectively brought all economic cooperation between Russia and the United States to a complete halt, inflicting serious damage primarily on the US economy and global markets," he wrote in a post on X.He added, "Economic cooperation between Russia and the United States serves the interests of both nations, contributes to global economic stability, and lays the foundation for building trust and achieving lasting peace."The legislation, backed by the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina and Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal, was designed to intensify pressure on Russia over its invasion of Ukraine in 2022."Instead of sanctions and confrontation, we need dialogue, mutually beneficial cooperation, and shared responsibility for global stability," Dmitriev wrote.The legislation sought to authorise sanctions against Russian officials and banks, as well as vessels linked to the country's shadow fleet of oil tankers. It also provided for tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from major importers of Russian oil and gas, including countries continuing to purchase Russian energy or helping Moscow evade sanctions.China and India, two of the biggest buyers of Russian oil, had raised concerns over the proposed measures. Beijing opposed what it described as "long-arm jurisdiction that lacks a basis in international law", while New Delhi warned that additional tariffs could affect bilateral ties.Trump's waiver drew criticism from US Representative Don Beyer, a Virginia Democrat, who accused the president of conceding to Moscow."Trump's latest surrender to Putin again betrays our Ukrainian partners and defies clear congressional intent of legislation designed to punish Russia for its illegal war of aggression," Beyer said in a statement.Trump said in the executive order that he had submitted a certification to Congress confirming that the waiver was in the US national interest. The suspension will remain in effect until Trump or senior officials determine that further action is appropriate.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Sri Lanka hit by nationwide power blackout as grid failure disrupts electricity
articles.summary: Sri Lanka suffered an islandwide power outage from around noon on Saturday, with the blackout continuing for more than three hours, power officials said.
articles.body: Sri Lanka suffered an islandwide power outage from around noon on Saturday, with the blackout continuing for more than three hours, power officials said.Water supplies, internet services and mobile connectivity were affected as authorities worked to restore electricity across the island in stages.The outage disrupted essential services, with the water supply agency warning people against wasting water as the power cuts could affect supplies.The cause of the islandwide outage was not immediately clear, although the government said a failure at a hydropower station in the central hill country, detected a day earlier, could have contributed to it.He urged rooftop solar panel owners to keep their systems disconnected from the grid until the power network was stabilised and electricity supplies restored, according to the state-run utility.The minister said a failure at a hydropower station in the central hill country, detected on Friday, could also have contributed to the blackout, PTI reported.You use AI every day. articles.title: US claims Iran unable to fund 'proxy militia' after losing $25 billion in oil exports to naval blockade
articles.summary: The US on Friday claimed Tehran was under severe financial pressure and unable to fund its proxy militia because of the naval blockade imposed by
articles.body: The US on Friday claimed Tehran was under severe financial pressure and unable to fund its proxy militia because of the naval blockade imposed by Washington.US central command (Centcom) commander, admiral Brad Cooper, claimed the financial crunch was because the US had blocked Tehran's access to sea routes.“Iran has no exports or imports by sea. The sum total of these actions has imposed a devastating cost on Iran’s security apparatus and IRGC specifically," Cooper said."In recent months, Centcom in close coordination with US agency partners has delivered severe blows to the Islamic regime and the IRGC in three important areas,” he added.Centcom claimed Tehran lost $25 billion since the blockade affected oil exports.Additionally, the US claims to have frozen Iran's $350 million in cryptocurrency, ANI reported.Iran's "proxy militia" includes members of the Axis of Resistance, a network of Iran-aligned governments and armed groups in the Middle East that oppose Israel and US military influence in the region. Its principal members and partners include Iran, Hezbollah in Lebanon, the Houthis in Yemen, Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad in the Palestinian territories, among others.The Centcom commander said Iran was facing shortages across several sectors, including energy and oil, steel and heavy industry, manufacturing, automotive, aviation, construction, security and the military.He asserted US dominance over the Hormuz region.“In seven days alone, 400 ships have sailed through the Strait. US has also assisted Gulf partners in shipping over 100 million barrels of crude oil during the same period, adding to more than 1.3 billion barrels we have helped allies to ship in the recent months,” Cooper said.The claim came amid competing assertions of control over the strategic waterway. On Friday, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said an “illegal supertanker” carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil had been struck by a sea mine while attempting to cross what it described as the “unauthorised” Strait of Hormuz.Iran’s ISNA news agency reported that the incident triggered an explosion and a severe fire. According to the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) weekly review, 135 such incidents have occurred in the Strait amid the Iran-US conflict.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: By 2020, an eastern Washington historian had spent more than 30 years building his own Monticello; the replica was about 90% complete and he was still working
articles.summary: Explore how historian Dan Sisson dedicated over 30 years to construct Monticello West in Washington using 22,186 salvaged bricks, inspired by Thomas Jefferson's Monticello.
articles.body: The house stands south of Ford, a small community in Stevens County, Washington, on land between state property and the Spokane Indian Reservation. Its brick walls and front elevation follow Thomas Jefferson’s Monticello in Virginia, though it was built with scavenged materials rather than a contractor’s budget. The builder is Dan Sisson, a historian, author, and longtime Eastern Washington University professor. He calls the house Monticello West. Though largely complete, the house remains a work in progress. The Spokesman-Review and the Los Angeles Times both covered Sisson’s project, and InsideHook later summarized the Times profile. Together, the reports describe a project that would normally take a construction crew, which Sisson took on with help from family, friends, and some hired workers, using mostly salvaged and secondhand materials.From Jefferson scholar to congressional candidate in 1976According to his biographical note, Sisson was born in Washington, D.C. He holds a master’s degree and a PhD. The note adds that he ran for Congress in 1976. A summary of that profile says he visited Monticello as a child with his father, who said that any building he made should resemble it.Digging the foundation at 61 and still working at 82A Los Angeles Times profile reports that Sisson dug the foundation with a shovel and pickaxe at 61 and was 82 when the profile was published. The profile also reports that he designed Monticello West in the mid-1980s, bought the land near Ford in 1998, and moved in during 2002.The Los Angeles Times article “How do you build a replica of Monticello? Brick by scavenged brick” reported that the replica, known as Monticello West, was about 90% complete by April 2020. Over two years, Sisson collected about 30,000 used bricks from a Spokane redevelopment zone, making roughly 120 trips in a pickup that could carry up to 250 bricks at a time. Stevens County withheld permission for the project until Sisson showed his plans to the planning director.Scavenged wood, flooring and marble, and thousands of straightened nailsMaterials were the project’s biggest challenge. Contemporary reports say he scavenged wood, flooring, and marble, much of it free or cheap, and straightened thousands of old nails for reuse. His wife and son helped, as did other people drawn to the idea of a Monticello northwest of Spokane.Jefferson’s plan in 1792 to reuse about 60,000 bricksReusing brick is not a new habit at Monticello. In a letter from Thomas Jefferson to Stephen Willis, 12 November 1792, Jefferson wrote that he expected the demolition of old walls and an antechamber to yield about 60,000 bricks. The Thomas Jefferson Foundation’s Monticello Encyclopedia records that Stephen Willis, a brick mason, arrived at Monticello around 1770 to help build the South Pavilion and continued working there through 1778. In effect, Jefferson reused materials from one project to build another, much as Sisson did with salvaged bricks.Jefferson’s 13 May 1822 brick estimate for six West Portico columnsJefferson also worked out his brick needs on paper. In Thomas Jefferson’s Notes on Bricks Needed for Monticello Columns and Cisterns, dated 13 May 1822, he tallied headers and stretchers course by course for six Doric column shafts. The editors identify those shafts as belonging to the West Portico. Monticello Magazine reports that the West Portico columns were restored in 2013 to their original look during Jefferson’s time by stripping away the layers of white paint and restoring the original render with period-appropriate materials. The restored columns are built of molded brick finished with a render, a cheaper approach than solid stone. Both builders, separated by two centuries, solved the column problem by choosing a cheaper material and shaping it to fit.Jefferson’s construction timeline and Sisson’s approach Sisson himself draws the comparison. Sisson himself draws the comparison, telling the Spokesman-Review that Jefferson spent 43 years building his house, a span he offers as a parallel to his own long schedule. The earlier-mentioned letter from 1792 indicates the pace at which Jefferson was proceeding. In 1792, Jefferson planned the next phase of construction at Monticello, including digging the cellars in early April.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Dhanbad Durga Puja pandals highlight tribal culture and sustainability
articles.summary: Dhanbad Durga Puja pandals at Steelgate, Jharkhand Maidan and Housing Colony showcase tribal culture with eco-friendly materials and seed-based idols.
articles.body: Dhanbad: Tribal culture, indigenous traditions and environmental conservation are at the heart of this year’s Durga Puja celebrations at three major pandals in Dhanbad. Organisers at Steelgate in Saraidhela, Jharkhand Maidan in Hirapur and Housing Colony are creating thematic pandals inspired by tribal lifestyles, traditional architecture and cultural heritage, while using eco-friendly materials to promote sustainability.At Steelgate, the Durga Puja committee is recreating elements of tribal life through artistic depictions of traditional homes and rural settings. Committee member Rajesh Mandal said, “The theme aims to familiarise visitors with the rich cultural heritage of indigenous communities.” Sculptor Ratan Mandal from West Bengal’s Medinipur district is crafting a unique idol of Goddess Durga using fruits, vegetables and a variety of seeds.The Sri Sri Satyam Shivam Sundaram Durga Puja Committee at Jharkhand Maidan is showcasing the tribal culture of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Installations made from natural materials will depict the lifestyle, customs and traditions of indigenous communities from the islands.The Sri Hanuman Mandir Durga Puja Committee at Housing Colony is preparing a tribal-themed pandal featuring an image of Goddess Durga atop the entrance and four horses on either side to welcome devotees. Bamboo, wooden strips, jute and foam are being used in its construction. Artisans from West Bengal have been working on the structure for nearly a month, while local artists are handling the illumination.By blending religious devotion with cultural awareness and environmental messaging, the three pandals seek to introduce visitors to indigenous traditions while encouraging the use of sustainable materials in festive decorations.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news.
